rubrics.rubric: Does SOCI201_EarlyAlert_Week10.xlsx calculate every student's projected grade correctly as of October 21, 2024?
criterion: Every student in the students table appears in the projected-grades area.
All eight grading components are shown with their Grading_Criteria weight.
All eight grading components are shown with their Grading_Criteria point value.

Attendance & Participation is treated as an interim Completed component when a score can be calculated from valid attendance and participation records through October 21, 2024, notwithstanding its Ongoing due-period label.
Each of the other seven components is marked Completed only when its dated due date is on or before October 21, 2024 and a grade is present.
Every other component is marked Pending.
Every Pending component is excluded from the projected-grade denominator.
The projected-grade calculation uses the displayed completed-component scores and weights consistently.
The treatment of Attendance & Participation is documented from the attendance and participation records.
Each student row displays any data-quality flag that affects the calculation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the workbook validate the attendance and assignment records and document every material anomaly with its calculation effect?
criterion: Every attendance record is linked to a rostered student.
Every attendance record has a usable class date.
Every attendance record has a recognized attendance status.
Every attendance record is checked for duplication.
Every attendance record is checked against the October 21, 2024 report date.
Every attendance record is checked for consistency with the course data.
Attendance records after October 21, 2024 are not used in the Week 10 attendance calculation.
Every material attendance anomaly is logged with table, record, field, value, issue, resolution, and effect on calculations.
Every assignment submitted_date is compared with its due_date.
A submitted_date after due_date is counted as late.
A missing submitted_date is counted as unsubmitted or missing.
Every material assignment anomaly or resolution is recorded in the data-quality documentation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the at-risk matrix evaluate every student against all eight source thresholds exactly as written?
criterion: Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Attendance Rate.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Assignment Completion.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Current Grade.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Midterm Exam Score.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Participation Score.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Missing Assignments.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for Late Submissions.
Every rostered student has a measured value and triggered status for No Office Hours Visits after the Midterm Exam date.
Each triggered status applies the threshold in the At_Risk_Criteria sheet without changing its comparison operator.

rubrics.rubric: Does the workbook provide a visible priority-weighted composite risk score and usable severity tiers?
criterion: A numeric weight is stated for each High, Medium, and Low priority level.
Higher-priority indicators receive at least as much weight as lower-priority indicators.
Each student's component contributions are visible.
Each student's composite score can be reproduced from the displayed contributions.
At least three non-overlapping risk-score ranges are defined.
Every student is assigned to the tier corresponding to the displayed score.

rubrics.rubric: Does the monitoring list apply the instructed buffer ranges without duplicating students already at risk on the same indicator?
criterion: Percentage-based indicators use a range from the at-risk threshold through five percentage points above it.
Participation uses the 5.0 through 5.5 range.
A student already at risk on an indicator is not also listed as monitoring-only for that indicator.
Each monitoring entry includes the student, indicator, measured value, and applicable range.
The monitoring population is derived from the same source values used in the at-risk matrix.

rubrics.rubric: Does the sociological analysis use student-por.csv correctly and state the limits of applying it to SOCI 201?
criterion: The analysis identifies the UCI Machine Learning Repository Portuguese secondary-school dataset as its source.
Family-background variables are related to G1, G2, and G3 using displayed calculations or summaries.
First-generation status is operationalized as Medu and Fedu both less than or equal to 1.
The Medu and Fedu coding is stated.
The first-generation operationalization is identified as a proxy.
The analysis explains the educational-level limit on generalization.
The analysis explains the country-context limit on generalization.
The analysis explains the meaning limits of studytime, famsize, Pstatus, and the 0–20 grade scale.
Findings are framed as group patterns rather than predictions for individual SOCI 201 students.

rubrics.rubric: Does Holistic_Intervention_Plan.docx connect individual risk evidence to cited WWC practices and feasible tiered supports?
criterion: Every at-risk student has an individual summary of triggered indicators.
Every at-risk student has an individual summary of the composite score.
Every at-risk student has an individual summary of relevant data-quality caveats.
Intervention strategies cite specific recommendations from Effective_Advising_Practice_Guide.pdf.
Academic and non-academic support services are distinguished.
Support intensity increases with the workbook's risk tier.
Each tier has concrete actions.
Each tier has a stated intervention timing.
Each tier identifies an owner.
Each tier defines follow-up.
The plan addresses realistic staffing, scheduling, privacy, or student-engagement constraints.
The sociological findings inform program design without being used to predict an individual student's outcome.

rubrics.rubric: Do both deliverables contain the required content areas, plan sections, and differentiated outreach materials?
criterion: The workbook contains clearly labeled projected grades, data-quality documentation, at-risk matrix, risk scores, and monitoring list content areas.
The workbook uses the exact required filename.
The intervention plan contains all six required sections.
The intervention plan uses the exact required filename.
Outreach templates are differentiated for materially different student risk or support needs.
No required deliverable or content area is replaced by a summary-only placeholder.
